messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak yesterday we're seeing a KV cache miss spike on prod canaries. I ran an nsys trace and ~12% of wall time looks to be profiler overhead; lots of time in a 'switchback' kernel. Thoughts on safe sampling vs full capture in prod?

maria: Can you paste the nsys CLI you used and the resulting trace size? Also what window did you capture? :eyes: 

alex: CLI I used:
````
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --sample=none --trace=nvtx,cuda python serve.py --workload=kv-heavy
````
Trace ended up ~1.2GB for a 30s run (nsys summary). Root timeline shows repeated switchback_kernel spikes correlated with batch formation.

jay: 12% overhead is believable if you captured syscalls + full CUDA stacks. For safe-prod I usually recommend sampling: e.g., 1s capture every 30s or perfetto short-samples. That typically drops overhead to ~0.5-1%.

perf-bot: automated: trace_size=1.2GB, events=42M, top_cuda_kernels=["switchback_kernel","kv_merge"], capture_window_s=30

samira: Agree with Jay. Also propose a hard guardrail: if trace_size > 200MB then abort upload and fallback to sampling-only capture. And we should emit a low-cardinality KV cache hit-rate histogram to Console so we can correlate without always doing full traces.

alex: The tricky bit: we need kernel timelines to correlate switchbacks with batch formation moments. Sampling risks missing rare long-tail switchbacks. Any mitigation ideas?

maria: Hybrid approach: lightweight periodic full-capture but only from a canary subset (10% of requests) + always-on telemetry (short histograms + span counters). For reproductions we can run deterministic seeds and small synthetic inputs to force the path.

jay: Add NVTX markers for batch boundary and kv-lookup start/end in the runtime. Then do targeted nsys captures that are NVTX-range-triggered (capture only when marker sequence seen). That reduces captured noise drastically and focuses on the interesting window.

alex: That sounds promising. Actionable plan + owners?

samira: I can add the KV hit-rate histogram and NVTX markers (tiny runtime change) — will open a PR by EOD. I'll also implement the local guardrail: profiler-controller checks /tmp/trace_size after capture and toggles sampling if >200MB.

maria: I'll draft the sampling policy doc: "1s full-capture every 30s on canary, abort if >200MB, fallback to event-only trace" and include retention/PII scrub rules. PR tomorrow.

jay: I'll prototype the NVTX-triggered capture helper and a perfetto-lite config. Example quick commands to iterate: 
````
# NVTX-range capture (nsys):
nsys profile -o trace.nsys --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda python serve.py
# perfetto-style short sampling (pseudo): sample 100ms every 5s
````

alex: Also want an automated regression alert: if KV miss rate > 2% for 5m, flip on canary captures. Can we add that?

perf-bot: alert rule created: kv_miss_rate>2% for 5m -> enable_canary_capture

maria: Quick security note: captured traces must have TTL 7d and be scrubbed of any keys/ids before upload to shared buckets. I'll add that to the sampling policy.

alex: Awesome. I'll upload the scrubbed nsys output link once PRs land. Thanks all :thumbsup:
